# buildkite_workload_identity (Resource)

A workload identity lets a workload, such as a job running on a Buildkite agent, call the Buildkite REST API
without a stored API access token. The workload exchanges an OIDC token from its identity provider for a
short-lived API access token, using the workload identity's `client_id`.

Buildkite only mints the access token when the OIDC token matches the workload identity's issuer, audience,
subject, claims, and claim conditions. The access token's scopes are limited to `grantable_token_scopes`,
and the pipelines it can reach to `resource_grants`. Changes to these only apply to access tokens minted afterwards.
Learn more in [Workload identity federation](https://buildkite.com/docs/apis/workload-identity-federation).

The API token's user must be an organization administrator, and the token needs the
`read_workload_identities`, `write_workload_identities`, and `delete_workload_identities` scopes.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "buildkite_organization" "current" {}

data "buildkite_pipeline" "release" {
  slug = "release"
}

# Let jobs in builds of the deploy pipeline's main branch create builds of the release pipeline.
# A job requests an OIDC token with:
#   buildkite-agent oidc request-token --audience https://api.buildkite.com/v2/organizations/<organization UUID>
resource "buildkite_workload_identity" "deploy" {
  name        = "Deploy pipeline"
  description = "Creates release builds from deploy jobs"

  oidc_issuer   = "https://agent.buildkite.com"
  oidc_audience = "https://api.buildkite.com/v2/organizations/${data.buildkite_organization.current.uuid}"
  oidc_subject  = "organization:acme-inc:pipeline:deploy:ref:refs/heads/main:commit:*:step:*"

  # Tokens from Buildkite jobs must be limited to your organization
  oidc_claims = jsonencode({
    organization_id = data.buildkite_organization.current.uuid
  })

  grantable_token_scopes = ["read_builds", "write_builds"]
  default_token_scopes   = ["read_builds", "write_builds"]
  max_token_ttl_seconds  = 600

  resource_grants = [{
    type   = "pipeline"
    access = "selected"
    ids    = [data.buildkite_pipeline.release.uuid]
  }]
}

# Let the report step of the release pipeline read builds and their logs from every pipeline,
# in builds of the main branch or a release branch
resource "buildkite_workload_identity" "release_reports" {
  name        = "Release reports"
  description = "Reads build results for release reports"

  oidc_issuer   = "https://agent.buildkite.com"
  oidc_audience = "https://api.buildkite.com/v2/organizations/${data.buildkite_organization.current.uuid}"
  oidc_subject  = "organization:acme-inc:pipeline:release:ref:refs/heads/*:commit:*:step:report"

  oidc_claims = jsonencode({
    organization_id = data.buildkite_organization.current.uuid
  })
  oidc_claim_conditions = "claims.build_branch == \"main\" || claims.build_branch.startsWith(\"release/\")"

  grantable_token_scopes = ["read_builds", "read_build_logs"]

  resource_grants = [{
    type   = "pipeline"
    access = "all"
  }]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `description` (String) A description of the workload identity.
- `grantable_token_scopes` (Set of String) The API scopes that access tokens from this identity can have, such as `read_builds` and `write_builds`. A workload can request a subset of them. Only some scopes are available to workload identities; `graphql` is not.
- `name` (String) The name of the workload identity.
- `oidc_audience` (String) The audience (`aud`) that OIDC tokens must include.
- `oidc_issuer` (String) The issuer (`iss`) that OIDC tokens must have. For example, `https://agent.buildkite.com` for Buildkite jobs.
- `oidc_subject` (String) The pattern that the OIDC token's subject (`sub`) must match, where `*` matches any characters. For example, `organization:acme-inc:pipeline:deploy:ref:refs/heads/main:commit:*:step:*` matches every job in builds of the `deploy` pipeline's `main` branch. For better security, restrict the subject as much as possible: a broad subject lets workloads that you didn't intend mint API access tokens for your organization.

### Optional

- `allowed_ip_addresses` (String) Space-separated IP addresses in CIDR notation that access tokens from this identity can be used from. If not set, they can be used from any address.
- `allowed_token_exchange_ip_addresses` (String) Space-separated IP addresses in CIDR notation that workloads can exchange OIDC tokens from. If not set, workloads can exchange tokens from any address.
- `default_token_scopes` (Set of String) The scopes that an access token has when its workload requests none. Must be a subset of `grantable_token_scopes`. Defaults to none, so workloads must request scopes.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether workloads can exchange OIDC tokens for access tokens. Disabling the identity revokes its access tokens. Defaults to `true`.
- `jwks` (String) If the issuer doesn't support OIDC discovery, the JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) to verify OIDC tokens with, as an HTTPS URL or inline JWKS JSON. If not set, Buildkite discovers the keys from the issuer.
- `max_token_ttl_seconds` (Number) The longest lifetime, in seconds, of access tokens from this identity. An access token never outlives the OIDC token it was exchanged for. Defaults to `3600`.
- `oidc_claim_conditions` (String) A [CEL](https://cel.dev) expression that OIDC tokens must also satisfy. Use it for more complex checks, such as a list of allowed values or a branch prefix. For example, `claims.build_branch == "main" || claims.build_branch.startsWith("release/")`. Learn more in [Write claim conditions](https://buildkite.com/docs/apis/workload-identity-federation#write-claim-conditions).
- `oidc_claims` (String) Top-level claims that OIDC tokens must have, as a JSON object of each claim and its exact value. For example, `jsonencode({ organization_id = "<organization UUID>" })`. Values must match their JSON type too, so `"42"` doesn't match `42`. For tokens from Buildkite jobs, include an `organization_id` or `organization_slug` claim. Up to 10 claims are allowed.
- `resource_grants` (Attributes List) The resources that access tokens from this identity can access, with at most one grant for each type. Defaults to none, so access tokens can't access any pipeline. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resource_grants))

### Read-Only

- `client_id` (String) The Client ID of the workload identity.
- `uuid` (String) The UUID of the workload identity.

<a id="nestedatt--resource_grants"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resource_grants`

Required:

- `access` (String) Which resources to grant: `all`, including those created later; `selected`, the resources in `ids`; or `none`.
- `type` (String) The type of resource to grant. Only `pipeline` is supported.

Optional:

- `ids` (Set of String) The UUIDs of the resources to grant. Required when `access` is `selected`, and not allowed otherwise. Up to 20 pipelines can be selected.

## Import

Using `terraform import`, import resources using the `id`. For example:
```shell
# Import a workload identity using its UUID
#
# You can find the UUID from the REST API response from:
# GET /v2/organizations/{org_slug}/workload-identities
terraform import buildkite_workload_identity.deploy 01a1b2c3-4d5e-7f60-8a1b-2c3d4e5f6a7b
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import instances using the `id`. For example:
```terraform
import {
  to = buildkite_workload_identity.deploy
  id = "01a1b2c3-4d5e-7f60-8a1b-2c3d4e5f6a7b"
}
```
